data.segment_description:
(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced. 
 (Pentagon: Martha Raddatz)  US-Iraqi plan for putting pressure on the insurgents in Iraq examined; scenes shown of American air strikes on Fallujah, which is controlled by insurgents & of a bombing in Ramadi; details given of bombings near Baghdad & Balad & the elements in the moves against the opposition.  [SAIS Foreign Policy Inst. Thomas KEANEY†- says the situation in Iraq is worse than a year ago.]  [Council on Foreign Relations retired Maj. Gen. William NASH†- comments on the plan's aim.] 
 (Studio: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced. 
 (Rochester, Minnesota: Dean Reynolds)  Campaign statement from Senator John Kerry on how the conduct of the war in Iraq is hurting the US at home featured; Democratic TV ad shown.  [KERRY&nbsp- says President Bush's wrong choices have left America without the resources needed at home; lists programs needing funding.]  [October 7, 2002, BUSH&nbsp- says Iraqi President Saddam Hussein is a homicidal dictator with weapons of mass destruction.]

data.segment_title: Campaign 2004 / Bush vs. Kerry / Bush's Military  Record
data.segment_description:
(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced. 
 (White House: Terry Moran)  The renewed debate about President Bush's National Guard service record examined; TV ad shown in which retired Air National Guard Lt. Col. Robert Mintz† says he never saw Bush at his Alabama unit; details given from Pentagon documents on Bush's service record & from a "Boston Globe" story about Bush's pledge.  [White House communications director Dan BARTLETT†- questions the Democrats' recycling old charges.]

(Studio: Peter Jennings)  President Bush's visit to Ft. Pierce, Florida, where Hurricane Frances struck & flooding from the tropical storm's rains shown.  The course of Hurricane Ivan updated; weather map shown.

data.segment_description:
(Studio: Peter Jennings)  A closer look at the federal assault weapons ban that will expire on Monday introduced. 
 (Los Angeles: Bill Redeker)  The impact of dropping the weapons ban examined; scenes shown of guns, ammunition & magazines; details given of the opposition of police to the weaponry.  [Ray's Sporting Goods owner Chuck PAYNE†- talks about high-capacity magazines.]  [Two gun ENTHUSIASTS&nbsp- back the end of the ban.]  [Los Angeles police Chief William BRATTON†- says they are weapons of murder.] 
 (Studio: Peter Jennings)  National Annenberg Election Survey findings on Americans' position on renewing the ban outlined on screen. 
 (Washington: John Cochran)  The politics of the gun legislation examined; details given of a report that the NRA will endorse President Bush after the ban expires & why the Democrats are not acting.  [July 26, former President Bill CLINTON&nbsp- accuses the Republicans.]  [Gun victim's mother Bryl PHILLIPS-TAYLOR†- questions Bush's stance.]  [NRA vice president Wayne LaPIERRE†- says a political bloc of Republicans & Democrats will keep the issue from seeing the light of day.]  [Earlier, Senator John KERRY&nbsp- backs the ban.] 
 (Studio: Peter Jennings)  Further coverage of the story on "Nightline" noted.

America Still at Risk (Railroads) Part II
data.segment_description: (Studio: Peter Jennings)  President Bush's changed position on a national intelligence czar & the intelligence  agencies' budget noted.   (Washington: Pierre Thomas)  The dangers posed by freight trains that carry lethal chemicals on the nation's railroads examined; details given of the capabilities for death from toxic clouds from a railroad car with an animated diagram of the spread of chlorine gas shown.  [Naval Research Laboratory Jay BORIS†- hypothesizes on a death rate from a toxic cloud.]  [Homeland security consultant Randall LARSEN†- says a terrorist could quickly cause a catastrophe.]  [Sierra Club Jim DOUGHERTY†- explains how the freight trains just sit on the tracks in Washington, DC.]  [Assn. of American Railroads Edward HAMBERGER†- cites the importance of the rail system moving this material.]  Rail security upgrades since 9/11 outlined.

(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Report introduced. 
 (New York: Ned Potter)  The return to earth of the Genesis space capsule featured; diagram shown of how the capsule was supposed to be captured on re-entry; scenes shown of the tumbling capsule without a parachute & of it embedded in the ground.  [Yesterday, helicopter pilot Cliff FLEMING†- says there's one chance.]  [Los Alamos National Laboratories Roger WIENS†, NASA Jet Propulsion Lab's Firouz NADERI†- comment.]
(Studio: Peter Jennings)  Tonight's "Peter Jennings Reporting From the Tobacco File: Untold Stories of Betrayal & Neglect" previewed.
